events.reason: Back pain flare, right groin burning

orders.reason: Right groin burning after back flare, possible upper lumbar radiculopathy

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-Day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
75 y/o F with long-standing lumbar osteoarthritis.

S: Lower back flared up after helping her grandson move furniture over the weekend. Since Sunday, a burning pain across the right groin, worse sitting. Feels the right leg is a little weak lifting it into the car. No saddle numbness, no bladder or bowel change. Walking normally. No fever, no rash in the area. Taking ibuprofen.

O: Afebrile, vitals normal. Gait steady, heel and toe walk normal. No rash. Abdomen soft, no hernia felt. Reflexes symmetric. Exam otherwise normal.

A/P: Burning groin pain with subjective hip weakness after a back flare, most consistent with an upper lumbar radiculopathy. No red flags. Urgent neurology referral placed; neurology can see her Thursday and will decide on imaging. Activity as tolerated, avoid lifting. Call for any numbness in the saddle area, bladder or bowel trouble, or worsening weakness.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient neurology, seen 5/7/2026. Reason for referral: right groin burning.

75-year-old woman with spinal osteoarthritis and chronic low back pain. Back pain worsened after moving furniture with her grandson. Burning across the right groin for 4 days, aggravated by sitting, slightly eased lying on her back; some difficulty lifting the right hip. Denies saddle anesthesia, bowel or bladder dysfunction and paresthesias in the legs. Walks without unsteadiness. Past history includes orthostatic hypotension and an anticholinergic medication reaction, both in the past.
Medications (per our intake list): amitriptyline 75 mg qhs, oxybutynin 5 mg BID, timolol 0.5% OU BID, ibuprofen 400 mg q6h prn. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: power 5/5 in all groups except mildly reduced right hip flexion. Reflexes symmetric and normal throughout. Decreased light touch and pinprick over the right inguinal area and upper inner thigh; sensation in the lower leg and foot normal. Rectal tone normal. Cranial nerves, coordination and gait normal.

Impression: uncomplicated right upper lumbar radiculopathy, likely root compression in the setting of lumbar spondylosis. No features of cauda equina.
Plan: MRI lumbar spine without contrast to look for foraminal narrowing. Will contact her with results and next steps.

documents.title: MRI done
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I had the MRI last Thursday. The neurologist's office called and said a nerve is pinched up high in my back and they want me to do physical therapy. My first session is next week. The burning is a bit better.

documents.title: RE: MRI done
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for letting me know. Physical therapy is a good plan. We have not received the MRI report yet; I'll go over things with you at your June visit.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up of right upper lumbar radiculopathy, seen by neurology 5/7.

S: Per patient, the lumbar MRI showed a pinched nerve high in the lower back; report not yet received here. Started physical therapy about ten days ago, twice a week plus home exercises. Groin burning less, comes mostly after sitting a long time. Hip feels stronger getting in and out of the car. No bladder or bowel change. Mood a bit lower with the pain but okay; PHQ-9 6. Still taking ibuprofen most days lately.

O: Vitals normal. Walks without limp. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Lumbar radiculopathy, improving with PT. Continue PT per neurology; will request the MRI report and neurology notes.
2. Depression: stable on sertraline 50, mild dip with the pain. Continue.
3. OAB on mirabegron, glaucoma on timolol: unchanged.
4. Chronic back pain: back to as-needed ibuprofen as the flare settles, with food.
5. Annual labs drawn today.
Follow-up in September.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs from Wednesday are all normal, including kidney function, blood count and cholesterol. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outpatient neurology follow-up, seen 7/8/2026.
Interval: MRI lumbar spine without contrast 5/21/2026 showed multilevel degenerative disc disease and facet arthropathy, with moderate right L1-L2 foraminal narrowing from a disc bulge and facet hypertrophy contacting the exiting right L1 root. No central canal stenosis. Conus normal. She has been in physical therapy since early June.
Now: groin burning much reduced. Exam: right hip flexion 5/5. Patchy reduced sensation persists over the upper medial thigh. Reflexes symmetric.
Impression: right L1 radiculopathy, improving.
Plan: continue home exercise program; follow up with neurology as needed.
